subject: Catalyze ISV: solution verification & reference sandbox
messages:
From: Laura King <laura.king@catalyze.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@catalyze.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Catalyze: request for reference sandbox validation

Hi Rachel / Sergio,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. We (Catalyze) are preparing a reference integration that uses Redwood Private in a VPC for our on-prem-ish customers. Before we start embedding the SDK into our deployment templates we need Redwood to run a short validation against the reference sandbox to confirm:

- compatibility with our multi-tenant routing (we will mirror tenant IDs)
- KV cache behavior across warm/hot start scenarios
- latency targets at 512-token sequences (p95 < 220ms preferred)
- quantized model fallback behavior (we may need INT4 profile suggestions)

I've attached a simple infra diagram and a CSV of the test matrix (catalyze-reference-arch-v1.pdf, catalyze-test-plan-2028-07.csv). Can you confirm the scope and who on your side will own the runs? Ideally we want a sign-off by the end of next week.

Cheers,
Laura King
Director, Product Integrations
Catalyze Inc.

Attachments: catalyze-reference-arch-v1.pdf (diagram), catalyze-test-plan-2028-07.csv (test matrix)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Laura King <laura.king@catalyze.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Catalyze: request for reference sandbox validation

Hi Laura — thanks for the detailed matrix and diagram. We're aligned on scope. Proposed approach:

1) Redwood runbook: we will run the reference validation from a dedicated sandbox in us-west-2 with a Private deployment profile that mirrors your VPC peering setup.
2) Test ownership: Karthik will lead connectivity and functional checks; Sergio will own perf/throughput and kernel/quantization checks; Marissa will run the integration smoke tests and doc the verification steps for your team.
3) Pass/fail criteria: we will use the thresholds in your CSV and the following additional checks: token-consistency across retries, cache-hit rate at 1k concurrent sessions, and model-fallthrough latency when using smaller quantized kernels.
4) Deliverables: test results CSV, annotated trace logs (redacted), and a short runbook with recommended config (redwood-sample-config.yaml).

Can you confirm desired test window dates? We can schedule runs starting Wed 2028-08-02 and provide a preliminary readout by 2028-08-04.

Thanks — rachel
Rachel Kim
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments to follow: redwood-sample-config.yaml (config stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Laura King <laura.king@catalyze.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Catalyze: request for reference sandbox validation

Laura / team — quick questions so I size the envs correctly:

- Do you expect warm KV cache reuse across tenant routings or strict isolations per tenant? (affects memory pressure and cache keys)
- Are you planning to use streaming responses in the reference integration? We'll need to toggle stream-on vs stream-off in the test matrix.
- For VPC connectivity, please share a temporary peering subnet or we can run via a controlled egress IP if that is easier for you.

Action: I'll prepare an infra blueprint and a terraform snippet for the peering. If you can share an ephemeral SSH key or a service account with limited scope, I can spin the sandbox on Tue morning and run the connectivity smoke.

Karthik
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Laura King <laura.king@catalyze.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 13:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Catalyze: request for reference sandbox validation

Adding perf notes — thanks Laura for the matrix. A few internal constraints + suggestions:

- Throughput target: to hit p95 < 220ms at 512 tokens we should test both batch-size=1 (low-latency) and batch-size=4 (cost-latency tradeoff). I'll capture token-level traces for both.
- Kernel selection: I'll exercise the attention optimization path and the fallback path. If the quantized INT4 profile shows elevated hallucination signals in your evals, we may recommend INT8 as a compromise.
- KV cache: we'll run a warm-up sequence of 30k tokens to prime cache layers and then run tenant-switch scenarios. Expect to iterate cache TTLs — we'll include suggested defaults in the runbook.

I'll also dump perf counters and a short summary doc. Targeting the perf run on Thu 2028-08-03 in your window.

— Sergio
Director, Applied ML Ops
Redwood Inference

> On Mon, Jul 30, 2028 at 10:03 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Can you confirm desired test window dates? We can schedule runs starting Wed 2028-08-02...

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@catalyze.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura King <laura.king@catalyze.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Catalyze: request for reference sandbox validation

Thanks team — confirming:

- We want tenant-isolated KV keys (Catalyze will namespace at the application layer), but common underlying cache is fine as long as keys don't collide.
- Streaming: yes, please include both streaming ON and OFF in tests; our control plane will exercise both.
- Peering: we'll provide a temporary peering subnet and a limited-scope service account for the runs (I'll send details via the Drive link).
- Acceptance criteria: p95 latency < 220ms, cache hit-rate >= 78% on warm runs, no correctness regressions vs baseline prompts (we included baseline prompts in the CSV).

I'll upload the peering snippet and a cropped topology to the Drive link by EOD. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Tom
Head of Integrations, Catalyze Inc.

Attachments: none

> On Mon, Jul 30, 2028 at 11:18 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> > If you can share an ephemeral SSH key or a service account with limited scope, I can spin the sandbox...

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Laura King <laura.king@catalyze.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@catalyze.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Catalyze: request for reference sandbox validation

Great — thanks for the confirmations. Final runbook and schedule below: 

- 2028-08-02: sandbox provisioning (Karthik) — infra + peering test
- 2028-08-03: perf and kernel experiments (Sergio) — batch-size=1/4, INT4/INT8 comparisons
- 2028-08-03 (afternoon): integration smoke (Marissa) — streaming on/off, tenant-switch flows
- 2028-08-04: deliverables (Rachel) — test CSV, traces (redacted), annotated runbook with recommended redwood-sample-config.yaml

Action items:
- Catalyze: share peering subnet + service account, baseline prompts (Tom) [due: 2028-07-31 EOD]
- Redwood: spin sandbox + provide SSH/service account for debugging (Karthik) [done: start 2028-08-02]
- Redwood: initial perf traces and config recommendations (Sergio) [deliverable: 2028-08-04]

If all looks good I'll post the runbook to the Drive link and we can treat the Aug 4th readout as the gating sign-off. Thanks everyone — looking forward to this being a repeatable reference for our ISV program.

Rachel Kim
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-sample-config.yaml (config stub)
